title: Carleson's Theorem for Continuous Periodic Functions

classical_carleson.statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{C}$ be continuous and $2\pi$-periodic. Then for almost every $x \in \mathbb{R}$ the partial Fourier sums converge to $f(x)$: $\lim_{N \to \infty} S_N f(x) = f(x)$, where $S_N f$ denotes `partialFourierSum N f`.
classical_carleson.sketch: The proof controls the exceptional sets where the partial Fourier sums stay far from $f$ using the weak-type estimate `rcarleson_exceptional_set_estimate_specific`: on a measurable set $E \subseteq [0, 2\pi]$ where the real-line Carleson operator of a bounded measurable function is at least $\delta$, one has $\delta\,|E| \le C \cdot C_{10.0.1}(4,2)\,(2\pi+2)^{1/2}|E|^{1/2}$; combined with the approximation constants (`C_control_approximation_effect'` and related helpers) this forces the exceptional set to have measure zero.
